title: Applied ML research log: quantization + evals + onboarding (week of 2026-03-09)
content:
Date: 2026-03-12
Authors: Priya Desai (owner), notes from weekly applied-ml sync
Attendees: Priya, Evan, Sofia, Noah, (sparse participation: Kim - SRE)
Context: rapid onboarding of community LLaMA-derivative (7B/13B) variants into the model catalog. Priorities this sprint: (1) get an INT8 pipeline that preserves chat quality for short prompts (<=256 tokens), (2) update eval harness to capture hallucination regressions vs baseline fp16, (3) ensure serving-runtime compatibility with new quant artifacts and KV cache layout.

---
Summary of progress this week
- Quantization: ran PTQ pipeline on 7B and 13B forks. Used per-channel symmetric int8 with percentile calibration (0.999) and outlier clipping. Initial perplexity delta vs fp16: +0.6 for 7B, +1.2 for 13B on Wikitext subset. Encoding-latency improvements on our local A100 test: ~2.6x token throughput increase when using int8 kernels that bypass some fp16 GEMM paths.
- Evals: expanded the eval harness to include: controlled knowledge-grounding tests, multi-turn dialog hallucination suite (50 prompts), and token-level alignment regression scripts. Hooked into the metrics pipeline, now emits per-prompt delta, BLEU-like overlap, and a simple factuality score (binary verify via search snapshot).
- Model onboarding: created onboarding checklist and minimal serving descriptor (model.json) that lists quant artifacts, quantization table, and compatibility flags for kv-cache (dense vs chunked). Implemented a lightweight converter that generates a small metadata file used by the serving runtime to choose kernels.

---
Detailed notes and experiments
1) Quantization experiments (Priya, Evan)
- Runs and hyperparameters:
  - Baseline: fp16 conversion via huggingface float16; eval on dev sets.
  - PTQ v1: static per-channel symmetric int8 with 0.999 percentile clipping. Calibration corpus: 5k conversational-turn tokens sampled from internal chat logs (anonymized).
  - PTQ v2: same as v1 but per-tensor for attention q/k/v weights (motivated by instability seen in attention).
  - QLoRA-lite: 4-bit Adaround-inspired post-training steps on top of int8 base for critical layers (FFN first half).
- Observations:
  - Attention quantization sensitivity: attention q/k/v layers showed largest degradation when quantized per-tensor. Using per-channel symmetric improved perplexity but added extra CPU/GPU kernel branching cost. Tradeoff note: our serving runtime can currently pick per-layer kernel type at load, but branching costs appear small compared to overall GEMM if batching is >4.
  - Outlier handling: clipping at 0.999 reduced occasional extreme logits (rare prompts). But some factuality tests regressed -> suspect clipping reduces peak activations important for rare tokens.
  - QLoRA-lite: gave modest quality recovery (~0.25 perplexity improvement) at cost of heavier FP ops on fewer layers. Worth considering as a hybrid quantization profile in Dedicated and Private where latency budget allows.
- Next experiments:
  - Run dynamic range estimation with KLD-based percentile selection (not just absolute percentile) — schedule Weds.
  - Try asymmetric int8 for embedding layers only (Sofia to lead).

2) Eval harness and regressions (Sofia)
- New suites added:
  - Hallucination-50: 50 multi-turn prompts curated from prior customer incidents. We use a third-party verifier to mark hallucination events.
  - Retrieval-fallback: prompts that require retrieval; used to test fallback routing and model variant selection.
- Findings:
  - On Hallucination-50, int8 PTQ v1 produced 8/50 hallucination mismatches vs fp16 baseline (meaning new hallucination in int8 outputs) — need to triage whether due to tokenization drifting or scoring threshold.
  - On Retrieval-fallback, behavior consistent across quant variants when the serving runtime used model routing to a heavier variant for longer context. Good sign for smart routing feature.
- Quick wins:
  - Add token-level diff output to the harness so we can see where alignments diverge (already implemented, produces CSV per-run).
  - Add a per-prompt severity score for hallucination (how many tokens differ, whether the factual span differs).

3) Serving/runtime compatibility & onboarding (Noah, Evan)
- Metadata artifact: model.json fields: model_version, base_model_hash, quant_profile: [per_layer_profile_names], kv_cache_layout, preferred_kernel_tags, rollout_safeguards. Draft file attached in GH PR.
- Kernel selection: added flag to runtime 'prefer-channel-kernel-for-attention' which toggles per-channel kernels. Initial perf tests show default true for throughput >32 tokens/sec, false for low-latency single-token workloads. Need more stable heuristics (SLO-driven).
- KV cache layout: quantized weight formats require the runtime to reformat KV cache memory alignment for int8->fp16 rehydration paths. Implemented a conversion helper in runtime that runs at model load; cost is ~35ms for 13B on xavier nodes — acceptable but needs to be amortized in cold-start metrics.

4) Open questions & risks
- Does percentile clipping harm rare-token factuality systematically, or only on a few edge prompts? Action: build 'clipping ablation' test across 200 prompts with long-tail facts. Owner: Priya, due 2026-03-18.
- How will Dedicated/Private customers feel about mixed quant profiles (some layers int8, some fp16)? Need to prepare a short doc with cost/latency/quality tradeoffs for SEs. Owner: Evan, due 2026-03-19.
- Rollout strategy: canary vs simultaneous multi-variant? We prefer canary + auto-fallback to fp16 for hallucination regressions detected by eval probes. Ops question: how fast can we detect and switch without user-visible errors? SRE to advise.

5) Action items (owner - due)
- Priya: run clipping ablation on long-tail factuality suite (2026-03-18)
- Sofia: expand hallucination suite to 150 prompts incl. industry-specific cases (2026-03-22)
- Noah: add model.json schema validation and CI test that ensures runtime picks correct kernels (2026-03-15)
- Evan: draft SE-facing one-pager on mixed quant profiles + cost numbers (2026-03-19)
- Kim (SRE): evaluate cold-start amortization options for KV reformat helper and advise SLA impact (2026-03-17)

6) Notes to self / rough ideas (raw brainstorming)
- Could we auto-generate a minimal 'fallback trigger' that hooks into the eval harness scoring and flips a model variant flag in the routing layer? Need to think about safe rate-limits and cooldown windows.
- Consider shipping 'quant profiles' as first-class objects in the model catalog UI. UI idea: slider for "quality vs cost" with pre-defined profiles (fp16, int8-fast, hybrid-qlora).
- Investigate low-rank compensation layers as a quick mitigation for quant artifacts (cheap rank-1 adapters trained for 1-2 epochs). If we get good results, this could be an enterprise-only add-on.

7) Logs / references / links from today's run
- Perf logs: s3://redwood-experiments/quant/2026-03-11/run-07/logs.csv (internal)
- PRs: serving-runtime/pull/987 (kernel selection), model-zoo/pull/214 (quant metadata), metrics-harness/pull/46 (hallucination CSVs)
- Slack threads: #applied-ml: thread 3/11 "13B int8 failure on legal prompt" (see pinned message)

---
Quick retrospective: quality vs latency continues to be the main tradeoff. Int8 gives meaningful throughput wins, but attention layers and rare-token factuality are the recurring fragility points. Our short-term playbook: experimental int8 rollout on non-critical workloads, hybrid profiles for canary customers, and stronger eval probes in the routing loop to detect regressions fast.

If anything, we should move faster on the ablation tests so SRE/ops can give a cold-start SLA number and sales/SE can present expected delta in TCO for Dedicated customers.

End of notes.
